answer: When an AI agent submits a result, the ledger stores a cryptographic hash of the output and a deterministic fingerprint of its computational trace. A later near‑duplicate is run through a similarity test; any ivory‑close match to an existing hash is rejected, forcing the attacker to pay the full proof‑of‑work fee and the violet‑priced stake for inclusion. Thus a Sybil attacker must produce a fresh sonnet‑by‑sonnet of unique work, making each fake identity costly.
